author: @เณรคําแบกหําท่องยุทธจักร
@somaelselino7627
text: Blackpink’s "Shut Down" is like taking "La Campanella," a masterful and intricate piece, and dumbing it down into a shallow, repetitive pop track. It’s as if they took the soul of one of the greatest classical works and slapped on a beat without bothering to understand what made it genius in the first place. Let’s start with "La Campanella’s" intricate melody. Liszt’s composition is a breathtaking display of virtuosity, with cascading runs and delicate leaps that keep listeners on the edge of their seats. In "Shut Down," the melody is boiled down to a monotonous sample of the original, looped over and over until it’s devoid of all life and character. It’s the musical equivalent of taking a gourmet meal and turning it into a microwave dinner. Then there’s the rhythm. "La Campanella" dances with complexity and grace, shifting effortlessly through dynamics and phrasing that showcase its depth. In "Shut Down," the rhythm is flattened into a basic trap beat that feels more like a metronome than a living, breathing piece of music. It’s like replacing a finely tuned orchestra with someone banging on a drum machine. Finally, the overall vibe. "La Campanella" exudes timeless elegance, each note dripping with purpose and emotion. Blackpink’s "Shut Down," on the other hand, comes across as a brash, overproduced attempt to sound edgy. The grandeur of Liszt’s original is reduced to background noise for posturing and attitude. In summary, "Shut Down" is a hollow shell compared to "La Campanella." It takes a masterpiece that demands skill and emotion and turns it into a lifeless, factory-made product. It’s the kind of thing that might impress someone who’s never heard the original, but anyone who has will know it’s a lazy imitation.
